_comment: Hand-maintained airline overrides, applied LAST by scripts/build-airlines.js and
therefore winning over every upstream source. Three reasons an entry belongs here:
1. COLLISION - the brand name a traveller types is claimed by more than one
carrier upstream, and the exact-match would pick the wrong (usually defunct)
one. Example: 'indigo' matches the dead US 'Indigo' (I9) rather than
'IndiGo Airlines' (6E), which is the airline anyone actually means today.
2. MISSING - the carrier is absent from the upstream sources entirely.
3. BRAND - the common short name differs from the registered legal name.
Every code here was verified against a fetched source (Virtual Radar Server
standing-data and/or Wikipedia 'List of airline codes'); 'src' records which.
Keys must be normalised the same way normName() does: lowercase, punctuation
collapsed to single spaces. Do NOT guess a code - a wrong one silently queries
someone else's flight, which is worse than no result at all.
Known still-missing (no source could verify a code, deliberately omitted):
Iberojet - claimed E9 elsewhere but unverified in both sources.

ajet.note: vs AJY row with empty IATA

play.note: Icelandic PLAY; absent from vrs, which still lists OG under Star Air. IATA verified from wikipedia, ICAO unconfirmed - only affects the adsb.fi call sign, never the schedule lookup.

wizz air abu dhabi.note: absent from vrs; ICAO unconfirmed (call sign only)
